lines.text: Six times! If everyone wants it, it's a sure thing.
That's herd behaviour. Everyone wanting it feels like proof.
In 1991, Jay Ritter studied IPOs from 1975 to 1984. Over three years, they lagged similar companies.
lines.say: In nineteen ninety-one, Jay Ritter studied I.P.O.s from nineteen seventy-five to nineteen eighty-four. Over three years, they lagged similar companies.

card.title: RITTER · 1991
card.body: IPOs from 1975–84 lagged similar firms over three years.

lines.text: And the ones from the busiest, hottest years did worst.
Wait, so it's a bad company?
That's not what it says. A crowd isn't information. Hype sets the price, not the value.
Just notice when everyone's buying is your only reason.
